title: TaskForce rules bundle, version 1
description: What an agent does alone, what is forbidden, what needs a person's decision, with who decided it, why, and when to review it. The rules without a layer are TaskForce's table; the rules of a company layer (workspace, project, process, role, person) can only make it stricter, and the floor of the engine comes after every layer. Evaluated by deterministic code only (see contracts/README.md).

project.description: The project of the work at hand, whose layer the bundle carries; null for the rules of the whole workspace.

process.description: The process of the work at hand, whose layer the bundle carries; null when the work follows no process.

digest.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the bundle without this field. Set by the server; the runner refuses a bundle whose digest does not match.

layers.description: The company layers the bundle carries, with the version and digest of each, for the record.

inverse.description: The action that undoes this one when it exists (delete-branch, close-pull-request, reopen-issue...). A reversible exit without an inverse is not reversible.

owner.description: The named person who answers for the rule.

layer.description: The company layer the rule comes from; absent for TaskForce's own table. A layer only makes the decision stricter: its allow never counts. A layer never decides harness.change, the action TaskForce owns: only its own table does.

text.description: The rule as the person wrote it, in words.

tool.description: Glob on the agent's tool name, for example Bash or mcp__taskforce__brain_search.

command.description: Glob on the parsed command: program and arguments joined by single spaces, for example npm test.

path.description: Glob on the file path, relative to the sandbox.

server.description: Glob on the key of the MCP server a company tool comes from.

actor.description: Who acts: an agent (Claude Code, Cortex, any agent) or a person in their own name. A missing actor is an agent.

over.description: A threshold: the condition holds when the named fact is a number greater than value.

fact.description: A numeric argument of a company tool, for example arg.amount.

ref.description: What the layer is for: the project id, the process key, the role (owner, admin, member) or the person's id; null for the workspace.

require.description: What an asking rule adds (R98): who may approve (any one of them), how many distinct people sign, and whether the person who prepared the action is kept out of the signers.
